🇲🇽📱 <u>MEXICO ASKS 1 MILLION TEACHERS ABOUT PHONES IN CLASS</u>

Before regulating cellphones in schools nationwide, Mexico's SEP will ask the people who actually run the classrooms: over 1 million teachers in more than 200,000 schools will weigh in on August 24-25. Sixteen states already have rules. The evidence behind the push is ugly — former Meta researcher Ravi Iyer notes 70% of young people feel manipulated by the platforms, and Meta's own internal research showed 13% of Instagram users aged 13 to 15 received unwanted sexual advances in a single week.
banner: CELLPHONES IN CLASS: MEXICO ASKS 1M TEACHERS

text:
🚨🇲🇽 <u>WEST PLANTS FAKE 'RUSSIAN ARMS TO NARCO' STORY — SVR</u>

Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service says a Western spy agency, working with Ukrainian operatives, is seeding Russian-made weapons captured on the Ukraine battlefield into Venezuela, Colombia and Mexico — backed by forged audio and video — to blame Moscow for arming Latin American cartels. The goal: poison Russia's ties with the region and drag its governments into the West's anti-Russia camp. The SVR calls it a "third-rate crime novel." The arms that actually flood Mexican cartels have a known origin, and it is not Moscow.
banner: INFO WAR: RUSSIA SAYS WEST PLANTS ARMS STORY

text:
🔥🇲🇽 <u>HUACHICOL FISCAL KINGPIN HEADED BACK TO MEXICO</u>

Rear Admiral Fernando Farías Laguna, accused of leading the Navy fuel-smuggling network that moved US fuel into Mexico through fake import schemes, is about to be transferred from Argentina to face Mexican justice. "Everything indicates there will be a transfer," Sheinbaum confirmed — he has been locked up in Buenos Aires since April, caught with fake documents after five months on the run. His brother, Vice Admiral Manuel Roberto, has been behind bars since September. No impunity, not even in the Admiralty.
banner: HUACHICOL FISCAL: ADMIRAL HEADS HOME IN CUFFS

text:
🇲🇽⚡ <u>MEXICO WON'T BE THE WORLD'S DATA FARM</u>

Sheinbaum drew the line on data centers: yes to what Mexico needs for its own AI development, no to turning the country into the server farm of others. "Mexico should not necessarily be the data center of other places in the world, because it requires a lot of energy, a lot of water," she said. Growth with "very little employment and a lot of natural resource consumption" is not the model. And the grid expansion behind it runs on a new mixed scheme — 54% public, 46% private — that keeps CFE in control.
banner: MEXICO: NOT THE WORLD'S DATA FARM

text: ‍BLOOMBERG: Mexico's Extortion Level Hits 11-Year High as Other Crimes Fall August 17, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Bloomberg found the one Mexican crime statistic going up and made it the headline. 🇲🇽 Same data, same week: homicides at an 11-year low, down roughly 40% under Sheinbaum, and 1,600+ extortion suspects detained since the government's anti-extortion strategy launched in July 2025. The decline made it in — as a subordinate clause.

text: ‍THE ATLANTIC: Influencers Are the Sinaloa Cartel's Newest Targets August 13, 2026 | 🟡 📰 The Atlantic's Kevin Sieff files the cartel-influencer feature, and the dek is more candid than most: "The U.S. is trying to destroy Mexican cartels. But so far, a turf war has only deepened." 🔍 Credit for naming who deepened it. What gets no magazine feature: Mexico's daily homicide rate just hit an 11-year low. The violence beat is weekly; the decline is invisible.
banner: Sinaloa Cartel Takes Aim at Influencers

text: ‍REUTERS/U.S. NEWS: Mexico's Braskem Idesa files for bankruptcy in US to reduce debt August 18, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Reuters ran the Braskem Idesa Chapter 11 filing straight: a pre-agreed plan cuts $920M+ in debt, senior debt drops from $2.5B to $1.6B, Braskem injects $476M and keeps control, exit expected in 60–90 days, operations uninterrupted. Context the wire skips: the Veracruz petrochemical complex's troubles trace back in part to Pemex's failure to deliver contracted ethane — a supply dispute AMLO renegotiated in 2019 after calling the original terms abusive.
banner: Braskem Idesa Files Chapter 11 in U.S.

text: ‍CNN: Americans could soon pay a lot more for strawberries. Here's why August 17, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Rare honest tariff math: the Trump administration's antidumping probe targets Mexico, source of 98% of US strawberry imports ($1B+ a year) — and the last time Washington slapped a 17% duty on Mexican tomatoes, prices jumped 12.8% in a year. 🍓 The Florida growers' counsel expects the hit to shoppers to be "relatively modest." Commerce's preliminary finding is due today. • "A whopping 98% of U.S. strawberry imports came from Mexico last year" • The tariff impact on consumer prices would be "relatively modest" — growers' counsel

‍LA TIMES: Mexico pitches a 'dry canal' land corridor as alternatives to troubled waterways August 17, 2026 | 🟡 📰 LA Times visits Mexico's $4B "dry canal" across Tehuantepec — 500+ miles of rebuilt rail, ports 36 hours from Houston, four days from LA — and files it under "serious doubts." 🚢 Same dispatch: Panama Canal waits have stretched to three weeks, Hormuz traffic is halted. The scenery does the editorializing: "muggy city," "weathered apartment blocks," "faded signs." The piece's own expert calls the project "a truly serious attempt." • "So far, there's serious doubts that it can be done." • "Global trade has a lot of inertia."
banner: Mexico's $4B Dry Canal Eyes Panama Traffic

text:
🇲🇽🥑 <u>AVOCADO EXPORTS FALL 25% AFTER US PRESSURE</u>

Mexico's avocado exports fell almost 25% in the first half of 2026, to $1.69 billion, El Financiero reports — a direct hit after Washington's repeated "phytosanitary" inspection suspensions in Michoacán. The world's top avocado exporter keeps learning the oldest lesson of living next to the US: your best customer is also your biggest extortionist. Market diversification is no longer a slogan.
